title: Tommy Ladnier roomed at her house
summary: Austin recalls Tommy Ladnier rooming at her house, his mother's death, and a cornet teacher.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Sidney Bechet: the man, the horn, the legend

blocks.x: When was the first time you met him, or when did you start working with him?
Well, Tommy roomed at my house when he first came to his cove. Oh, he roomed with you.
That's right. You told me that, or I heard that some reddit someplace.
Well, he and his mother lived over East End, and his mother got killed. Oh, I didn't know.
I never knew Tommy very well.
Well, his mother got killed, and some mother tried to say that he and his mother, he and some man was fighting, and he shot the man, and the shot killed his mother.
So they had him in trouble for a long time.

Then he came to room with the man. I was living in 33rd then. And he was playing connet. And you know this, I'm trying to think now, what is his name? He's a connet player. He has a band. I said, all right boy. Then he had a garage. What was his name? He taught that boy to play connet right into my house. And finally the boy got in the band. And I went to New York to see my father. That's the first time I went to New York. And one of the boys there that was from New Orleans said, love me, I'm getting ready to go to England. And I haven't got any connet player with that one. And he said, did you get Tommy to work with me? I said, I don't know, I'll find out.
